proof.criterion: The install block's cache guard fails a test when it is reverted — the reviewer's finding that it was pinned by nothing.
proof.surface: The rendered start wrapper, run under /bin/sh with stand-ins for bun and node, in this role container.
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox/ -run TestAnInstallRemakesAPoisonedCacheAndSparesARealOne -count=1 -v; then the same after editing installBlock back to the pre-guard shape; then jj restore of plugins.go
proof.observed: Four subtests pass at the head: a 0-byte regular file at $BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR is cleared and the path is a directory afterwards; a filled cache keeps entry.txt and nested.json byte for byte; a symlink to a filled cache is still a symlink with its target intact; a path with nothing at it runs clean. With `mkdir -p -- "$cache"` moved back outside legion_install and the `[ -d ] || rm -f` line removed, the first subtest fails: `the wrapper exited 1 with a regular file an interrupted flock left behind at the cache path … mkdir: cannot create directory '…/cache': File exists`. plugins.go restored from the parent commit and absent from the round's diff.
proof.negativeControl: The revert is the control and I ran it myself rather than taking the subagent's word, since the finding was precisely that a reported-green check proved nothing. The 'no cache at all' subtest is the second control: without it the three prepared cases could pass on a wrapper that never touched the path.

proof.criterion: Every directory the runtime renders onto the issue volume is accounted for in the operator's reclaim remedy, checked against the renderer rather than by a reader.
proof.surface: docs/kubernetes.md's reclaim paragraph, now two markdown lists, parsed by a Go test in the package that renders the paths.
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox/ -run TestTheReclaimParagraph -count=1, at the head and with the document mutated two ways
proof.observed: TestTheReclaimParagraphNamesEveryDirectoryTheRendererPutsOnTheIssueVolume derives nine directories from roleEnvironment and the issue pod's agentEnv and requires each on the delete list or opening an exemption bullet, in exactly one of the two; TestTheReclaimParagraphNeverDeletesWhatItExempts refuses a delete-list path that is an ancestor of an exempt one. My own controls at this head: removing the `/legion/uv/cache` bullet gives `accounts for /legion/uv/cache in neither list … a mention inside an exemption's reason is neither`; coarsening it to `/legion/uv` gives `deletes /legion/uv, which holds /legion/uv/python/<issue> that the same paragraph exempts … the bullet is a segment too coarse`. The document was restored by checksum after each (f3e94c63…).
proof.negativeControl: The first version of this test searched the paragraph's text and **passed** with /legion/uv/cache off the delete list, because an exemption's prose mentions the path. I found that with the control above, which is why the committed version parses the two lists and ignores a path named inside a reason. An unreadable document, a missing boundary marker, a region with no paths and an empty list are each a hard failure rather than a skip.

proof.criterion: The remedy's instructions are ones an operator can follow without harm: tmp's window matches its only creator, and the uv split protects what a workspace depends on.
proof.surface: docs/kubernetes.md read against EnsureScratch's callers and manifest.go's uv contract.
proof.command: grep -rn 'EnsureScratch(' packages/daemon --include=*.go; read manifest.go's uvPythonRoot comment; read the paragraph at the head
proof.observed: EnsureScratch has one non-test caller, worker_shim.go, run once as the shim starts Oh My Pi, so a role's shim outliving a turn means a deleted tmp stays gone until relaunch: the document now says to delete it with the role stopped, names the shim start as its only creator, and states both halves of a live role meeting a missing TMPDIR — `mktemp -d` exits 1, Python's `tempfile` silently falls back to /tmp, the container's own filesystem, re-arming the eviction this layout exists to prevent. 'A temporary directory' is out of the rebuilt-by-the-next-build clause, which now names only the caches. /legion/uv/cache is on the delete list and /legion/uv/python/<issue> is an exemption carrying the dependency manifest.go's uvPythonRoot promises: a project's .venv in the issue's workspace links to an interpreter there, and the remedy deletes no workspace.
proof.negativeControl: The reviewer ran the halves that matter and I did not re-run them: `mktemp -d` exit 1 and Python placing its directory at /tmp with TMPDIR naming a path that does not exist. What I checked independently is the claim the clause rests on — that EnsureScratch has exactly one non-test caller — since that is what makes 'between turns' the wrong window.

filesChanged: packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/plugins_test.go — TestAnInstallRemakesAPoisonedCacheAndSparesARealOne; runStart takes the cache path so a caller can say what is at it.
packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/live_setup_unit_test.go — one call site updated for that parameter.
packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/reclaim_doc_test.go — new: the two fences over the reclaim paragraph.
docs/kubernetes.md — the remedy is a delete list and an exemption list; tmp's window and its fallback hazard; uv split; the hand-maintained count dropped from the lead-in.
trickyParts: flock creates a missing lock path as a regular file and exits 0, which is why the pre-guard shape was a one-way failure rather than a transient one.

The fence's first version was satisfied by a path mentioned in an exemption's prose. The committed version parses the delete list and the exemption bullets structurally: a path counts only as a whole delete bullet or as the path an exemption bullet opens with.

The ancestor rule (a delete-list bullet covers what is under it) is needed for /legion/go to cover GOCACHE and GOMODCACHE, and is exactly what would let a coarsened bullet swallow an exemption — hence the second test.
discoveredComplexity: Both committed tests check structure, not grounds, and their comments say so: an earlier head passed a check of this kind while carrying an exemption whose stated reason the code refuted. Which of the two lists a path sits on is likewise a reader's judgement — a cache promoted into the exemptions passes. The fences stop the class of failure that recurred six times (a rendered path unaccounted for, a delete that swallows an exemption) and nothing beyond it.

This round's first fence was reported green by the subagent that wrote it and was too weak; my own control found that. The review's own lesson applied one level up: a check's author is the worst-placed party to judge whether it can fail, because the control they imagine is the one their design already handles.
